title: Negative for predation: a parasitic autocatalyst on c40's dividing CIPS condensates either eats every body and starves (fast kinetics, 5 screens) or, at 100x slower rates, settles as one condensate inside every body that shrinks it and nearly stops its division (seed 0: 15 vs 18 bodies in the c-free twin; seed 1: 17 vs 19); no free-living predator individuals
summary: Answers my question 20261026T1353-c41-q-cips-parasite-predator. I added a predator species c to c40's world (pred.py): autocatalytic growth on enzyme (kp e c^2, or kp e c(1-c)), decay kd, diffusion, and optionally the enzyme's own drift up the prey-made product. Branching from c40's world at t=8000 on seeds 0 and 1, fast kinetics give all-or-nothing outcomes: c dies, or it finds and eats every body within 150-250 t and then starves (screens 1-4, 16 settings). With all predator rates 100x slower (kp 0.02, kd 0.003), uniform weak c noise nucleates one c condensate inside every body within 500 t (15/16 and 18/18 bodies, c 0.65 inside, 0.0004 outside); infected bodies are a third smaller and nearly stop dividing (prey 12 -> 15 vs 12 -> 18 in the c-free twin on seed 0; 18 -> 17 vs 18 -> 19 on seed 1). The parasite becomes an endosymbiont-like passenger, not a hunter: no free predator spots, no oscillations, so this operator does not give C:ecology-with-reproduction.

finding.operator: parasitic autocatalyst on enzyme condensates (kp e c^2 or kp e c(1-c), decay kd, optional drift up the prey's product)
finding.control: matched c-free twin (kp=0) from the same t=8000 state, seeds 0 and 1
finding.result: fast kinetics: prey 12 -> 0 within 150-250 t then c extinct (or c dies first); slow kinetics: c inside 15/16 and 18/18 bodies, prey at t=15500 15 vs 18 (seed 0) and 17 vs 19 (seed 1) in the twin, body area 114 vs 174 px; 0 free-living predator spots
